scope: Finite source and reasonableness review for production object dialog; not whole ontology or runtime assurance
assessmentMethod: Check current applicability and precise supersession

records.sourceAuthority: Current versioned user-confirmed policy, supported by batch-process-2026-10-27.md; current user explicitly adopted new remote rules
records.currentApplicability: current; old work-order lock policy replaced in this claim only
records.reason: One object can explicitly identify the process that will run. Separating new candidates from existing references avoids silently switching configuration, while product-first/family-fallback supports shared and product-specific process ownership. It is a user product choice, not inferred from existing code or generic manufacturing rules.

records.currentApplicability: current; new independent process versions still require one production form per order
records.reason: A single BATCH/SN form keeps allocation and object quantity semantics coherent in this MVP. Mixed forms can be legitimate in other products, so the rule must not be elevated to an industry-wide invariant. Current feature scope contains no approved mixed-form flow.
implementationEvidence: WorkOrderPage fixedProductionForm and disabled incompatible options

records.sourceAuthority: Current versioned user-confirmed quantity policy; batch-process evidence explicitly records positive fractions allowed
records.currentApplicability: current; quantity lower-bound question was explicitly resolved, not left at historical >=1
records.reason: Positive quantity prevents empty/negative allocations; SN=1 matches individual serial identity; non-cancelled targets bounded by the plan prevent over-allocation. Planned and achieved quantities remain distinct, so scrap or early end does not silently create extra allocation. Four decimal places are a storage/engineering limit, not quoted user policy.

records.sourceAuthority: Versioned user-confirmed screenshot field contract; historical raw screenshot not retrieved in this review
records.currentApplicability: current; later batch-process correction did not replace this field contract; merged H008 matches it
records.reason: For one serial per object the quantity is redundant. A minimal canonical template with serial number and optional dates is internally consistent and can reduce incorrect quantity input. An optional remarks column could also be reasonable in another approved UX; three columns are correct here because of the current explicit user choice, not because four columns are inherently unsafe.
evidenceLimits: No claim of re-reading the historical screenshot or external Guancheng runtime
Canonical download format is distinct from tolerant input parsing

records.sourceAuthority: Original implementation evidence and narrowly scoped repair compatibility; not a new user-confirmed permanent-compatibility policy
records.currentApplicability: current accepted implementation boundary; unchanged by this layout work
records.reason: Keeping the existing optional remark parser does not contradict the three-column canonical download. It prevents an unrelated input capability from being removed while fixing layout/template output. It does not authorize every extra column or require indefinite compatibility with all old files; imported SN quantities other than one still fail validation.

records.currentApplicability: current for manual, generated and imported candidates
records.reason: A reviewable pending list lets users correct or remove candidates before allocations and audit history are created. It makes the final submit the clear persistence boundary, reducing accidental partial imports. Pending is UI state and does not invent a database lifecycle state.
implementationEvidence: WorkOrderPage split mutation and onSuccess pendingObjects reset

records.sourceAuthority: Current versioned user-confirmed atomic batch save
records.currentApplicability: current; applies to runtime writes and audit records, not merely a visual batch
records.reason: An all-or-nothing batch prevents users having to infer which allocations succeeded after a failed file or repeated submit. It also keeps creation audits aligned with saved objects. It has an expected large-batch cost, but performance work must preserve the accepted atomicity unless the user changes the workflow.

records.sourceAuthority: Current versioned user-confirmed preview and independent selection scope
records.currentApplicability: current; replaces the old work-order-locked selection interpretation
records.reason: A read-only preview explains the selected configuration without editing master data. Keeping selection separate allows creating a new object with another permitted version. Treating all controls as read-only because the preview is read-only would conflate two distinct responsibilities.
implementationEvidence: WorkOrderPage 本次添加使用的制程 and 预览当前配置 controls

records.sourceAuthority: Current versioned user-confirmed first-start freeze boundary, also supported by user's current adoption of remote policy
records.currentApplicability: current; not the withdrawn creation-time family freeze interpretation
records.reason: Editable unstarted allocations remain flexible, while prohibiting mutation after execution begins preserves the relation between actual production and its evidence. Checking execution existence as well as status protects against status-only bypass. Layout changes must not turn hidden controls into a new lifecycle permission.
implementationEvidence: ProductionExecutionService.act created START branch and requireApplicableProcess

conclusion: No policy or knowledge change needed for the proposed local layout repair. Nine finite records assessed; no blocking real business ambiguity found.
